chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
That the inheritance of the child of the mother cursed by her husband is for its mother. So if its mother was not alive, then it goes to the closest people to the mother, his maternal uncles.
ai.seo_question: Who inherits from a child of the cursed mother if the mother is deceased?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the inheritance distribution for the child of 'al-mula'ana' (where the husband and wife exchange oaths of cursing), establishing that the mother is the primary heir. If she has passed away, the inheritance transfers to her closest maternal relatives, specifically her maternal uncles (akhwal), reflecting the Shia juristic view that the paternal line is severed in this specific legal context. This ruling highlights the distinct Shia interpretation of kinship ties in cases of formalized marital dispute compared to other schools of thought.
